about: Army traditions (decisions 'Army traditions', 'How traditions form', 'Losing traditions'): history's traditions each people has at the start, plus ones earned by victories won chiefly by one arm or by cities taken. A tradition fades after 50 years without use and is lost in a crushing defeat of its arm. effects: might_<role> adds to that arm's fighting value; siege speeds sieges; skill_<skill> adds to new generals' skills. realms: only these realms of the culture. Sources: Polybius, Livy, Arrian, Diodorus; our own summary, free for any use.

traditions.name: The manipular legion
traditions.text: Rome's flexible lines of maniples, hastati, principes and triarii, that beat the Samnites in their own hills.

traditions.name: The fortified camp
traditions.text: Every night a Roman army dug a ditch and rampart round its camp; its officers learned engineering with the spade.

traditions.name: Phalanx and Companions
traditions.text: Philip's and Alexander's hammer and anvil: the pike phalanx holds, the Companion cavalry strikes.

traditions.name: Alexander's school
traditions.text: The Successors' generals learned war under Alexander and taught it to their sons.

traditions.name: The hoplite tradition
traditions.text: Citizens trained from youth to stand in the shield wall (Sparta's agoge above all).

traditions.name: Rhodian seamanship
traditions.text: The best sailors of the Hellenistic world, who kept the seas free of pirates.

traditions.name: Cretan archery
traditions.text: Crete's archers served every king of the age as mercenaries.

traditions.name: Masters of the sea
traditions.text: Phoenician and Carthaginian fleets ruled the western sea for centuries.

traditions.name: The Numidian horse
traditions.text: Riders without bridle or saddle, the finest light horse of the age (Polybius).

traditions.name: The warband's charge
traditions.text: The Gauls' terrible first rush, that sacked Rome and Delphi.

traditions.name: War in the hills
traditions.text: Iberian ambush and skirmish in broken country, that cost Rome two centuries.

traditions.name: Peltasts of Thrace
traditions.text: Thracian javelin men, the masters of light infantry since Iphicrates' day.

traditions.name: Illyrian raiders
traditions.text: The fast lembi of the Illyrian coast, raiders of the Adriatic.

traditions.name: Born in the saddle
traditions.text: Peoples who lived on horseback, every man an archer from childhood.

traditions.name: The Persian horse
traditions.text: The noble horsemen of Iran and Armenia, heirs of the Achaemenid cavalry.

traditions.name: Archers of Ta-Seti
traditions.text: Kush, 'the land of the bow' to the Egyptians.

traditions.name: Desert riders
traditions.text: Peoples who crossed the desert by camel, where armies of the river lands died of thirst.
